displayedInputs.question:
A circle of radius \(2\) is inscribed in a semicircle, as shown. The area inside the semicircle but outside the circle is shaded. What fraction of the semicircle’s area is shaded?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Triangle \(ABC\) has a right angle at \(B.\) Point \(D\) is the foot of the altitude from \(B,\) \(AD = 3,\) and \(DC = 4.\) What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

In quadrilateral \(ABCD,\) \(AB = 5,\) \(BC = 17,\) \(CD = 5,\) \(DA = 9,\) and \(BD\) is an integer. What is \(BD?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Four congruent rectangles are placed as shown. The area of the outer square is \(4\) times that of the inner square. What is the ratio of the length of the longer side of each rectangle to the length of its shorter side?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

The figures \(F_1,\) \(F_2,\) \(F_3,\) and \(F_4\) shown are the first in a sequence of figures. For \(n \ge 3,\) \(F_n\) is constructed from \(F_{n-1}\) by surrounding it with a square and placing one more diamond on each side of the new square than \(F_{n-1}\) had on each side of its outside square. For example, figure \(F_3\) has \(13\) diamonds. How many diamonds are there in figure \(F_{20}?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Many Gothic cathedrals have windows with portions containing a ring of congruent circles that are circumscribed by a larger circle. In the figure shown, the number of smaller circles is four. What is the ratio of the sum of the areas of the four smaller circles to the area of the larger circle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

A rectangular yard contains two flower beds in the shape of congruent isosceles right triangles. The remainder of the yard has a trapezoidal shape, as shown. The parallel sides of the trapezoid have lengths \(15\) and \(25\) meters. What fraction of the yard is occupied by the flower beds?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

Segment \(BD\) and \(AE\) intersect at \(C,\) as shown, \(AB=BC=CD=CE,\) and \(\angle A=\dfrac52\angle B.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle D?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: In the centered tangency configuration shown, the small circle's diameter equals the semicircle's radius. Circular areas then give the shaded fraction.
mappings.answerReason: The semicircle has radius 4 and area 8π. The inner circle has area 4π, so the shaded fraction is (8π - 4π)/(8π) = 1/2.

mappings.rationale: The required area uses hypotenuse AC = 7 as its base. Its altitude can be determined either from the similar right triangles or by combining Pythagorean identities in the three right triangles.
mappings.answerReason: Similarity gives BD² = AD·DC = 12, so BD = 2√3. Thus the area is (1/2)(3 + 4)(2√3) = 7√3. Alternatively, AB² + BC² = (9 + BD²) + (16 + BD²) = 49 gives the same altitude.

mappings.rationale: Diagonal BD belongs to two nondegenerate triangles. Their strict triangle-inequality bounds must hold simultaneously, and BD must be an integer.
mappings.answerReason: Triangle ABD requires 4 < BD < 14, while triangle BCD requires 12 < BD < 22. Their intersection is 12 < BD < 14, whose only integer is 13.

mappings.rationale: With rectangle sides L > W, the arrangement gives outer square side L + W and inner square side L - W. The square-area ratio determines L/W, either through positive square roots or by factoring the area equation.
mappings.answerReason: Let t = L/W > 1. Then (t + 1)² = 4(t - 1)². Positive side lengths give t + 1 = 2(t - 1), hence t = 3. Factoring instead gives (3 - t)(3t - 1) = 0, and t > 1 excludes 1/3.

mappings.rationale: The figure sequence requires generalizing the diamond count. Layer k has k diamonds per side, with shared corners counted once, so it adds 4(k - 1) diamonds.
mappings.answerReason: Starting with one central diamond, F20 contains 1 + 4(1 + 2 + ... + 19) = 1 + 4·19·20/2 = 761 diamonds.

mappings.rationale: The neighboring tangencies make the four small-circle centers a square of side 2r. Internal tangency relates the larger radius to the distance from its center to each small-circle center; the square diagonal and circle areas determine the ratio.
mappings.answerReason: Each small-circle center is r√2 from the larger center, so R = (1 + √2)r. The area ratio is 4πr²/(πR²) = 4/(1 + √2)² = 4(3 - 2√2).

mappings.rationale: The flower-bed area can be found by subtracting the trapezoid from the rectangle. Alternatively, the equal legs of the two isosceles right triangles determine their dimensions and areas.
mappings.answerReason: If the common height is h, the yard has area 25h and the trapezoid has area (15 + 25)h/2 = 20h. The flower-bed fraction is therefore (25h - 20h)/(25h) = 1/5.

mappings.rationale: Equal sides give equal base angles in both triangles. The triangle angle sum determines the left triangle's angles, and vertical angles transfer the angle at C to the right triangle.
mappings.answerReason: Since AB = BC, angle A = angle ACB = (5/2)angle B. Thus 6 angle B = 180°, giving angle ACB = 75°. Its vertical angle DCE is also 75°, and CD = CE gives angle D = (180° - 75°)/2 = 52.5°.
